business_problem: The bank wanted a proactive way to monitor a complex IT environment, predict critical service outages, and reduce the impact of infrastructure failures on customers and employees.
solution_summary: DXC worked with the bank’s IT team to build an AIOps-based predictive outage solution for a complex banking estate. Historical system-level log data and service-management metrics from hundreds of banking systems, including customer-facing platforms and back-end credit card and processing systems, were ingested and analyzed to identify patterns linked to future incidents. DXC data scientists used a design thinking process, SME interviews, workshops, and feature engineering to select and productionise 700 features inside the bank’s big data cluster. An AIOps model then continuously observes operating signals, generates outage likelihood risk scores, and feeds iterative learnings back into the model for ongoing accuracy improvement. The resulting predictions and next-best-action insights are surfaced in a dashboard so service managers can intervene before failures occur, and the same data also supports quarterly APRA regulatory reporting.

solution_components.name: AIOps model
solution_components.role: Continuously analyzes service-management and log data to generate future outage risk scores and support automated issue resolution activities.

solution_components.name: big data cluster
solution_components.role: Hosts the productionised feature set and underlying data used to train and run the predictive outage models.

solution_components.name: dashboard
solution_components.role: Presents advance warnings, risk insights, and next best actions for service managers to act on before systems fail.

data_flow: Historical log and service-management data from hundreds of customer-facing and back-end banking systems are ingested into the bank’s big data cluster, where 700 engineered features were productionised. The AIOps model analyzes three years of incident data, generates outage risk scores and next-best-action insights, and publishes warnings to a dashboard used by service managers and for APRA regulatory reporting.
integration_points: Australian Prudential Regulation Authority (APRA) regulatory reporting
business_outcome: The bank can predict high-priority incidents affecting customer-critical systems up to four weeks in advance, improve IT service management quality, reduce outage risk, increase resilience and reliability, and support quarterly regulatory reporting.
